transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Jun (Redwood SE), Karen (BlueBeacon Head InfoSec), Darren (Platform Eng), Maya (Legal Ops)

Summary:
- Security intake focused on whether Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private meets BlueBeacon regulatory and data-residency needs; primary asks: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC granularity, audit logs retention and format, encryption/BYOK KMS, and data retention/erasure controls.
- Customer leaning toward Dedicated with VPC peering or Private for highest control; wants proof of controls + test SAML flow before legal approval.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO plans
- SSO/SAML + SCIM integration testing
- RBAC, token/session controls and least-privilege roles
- Audit logs: fields, retention, export/streaming (SIEM integration)
- Encryption: at-rest AES, KMS BYOK/HSM options, key rotation, split trust
- Data retention policies, legal hold, deletion workflows
- Deployment options: Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Pilot next steps and legal exchange

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, imperfect ASR):
[00:00] Aisha: All right, hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is Aisha from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Say hi?
[00:06] Karen: Hi, Karen here, Head of InfoSec at BlueBeacon. Thanks for fitting us in, we're trying to get security gates in place for a Q1 pilot.
[00:12] Miguel: Hey Karen, Miguel on the SE side, i'll walk through how the stack can meet the controls you called out. Jun's on in case we need deeper infra specifics.
[00:20] Darren: Darren here, i'm our platform engineer, i'll be owning the integration work on our side. Quick note, we have strict PCI scoping for any tokens we store.
[00:29] Jun: quick wave, Jun.
[00:31] Maya: Maya from legal. We'll be handling the DPA / processor review.
[00:35] Aisha: Cool, quick agenda — SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS details, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:41] Karen: Yep. First up SOC2. Where are you on SOC2 and ISO? We need Type II report or at least evidence for controls.
[00:48] Miguel: We have SOC2 Type II for the inference platform, latest report is 2025 August — i'll share the attestation. ISO 27001 is in progress, cert expected Q2 2026, but we can provide the scope and audit plan.
[01:02] Karen: Okay, we'll want the actual report for our vendor risk team, redacted as needed. Also do you have penetration test summaries and change-management controls?
[01:10] Jun: we do annual pentest summary and internal change control docs; SE can share summaries, the full pentest might be redacted in places.
[01:18] Aisha: I'll include the pentest executive summary in the packet.
[01:21] Maya: From legal, any standard subprocessor list? We need to check where logs and backups live.
[01:26] Miguel: Subprocessors include cloud infra providers for hosted, and partner network for dedicated capacity; we'll give a list and the default regions. For Dedicated/Private, you can restrict to your VPC/region.
[01:36] Darren: Could you be explicit about where audit logs are stored and how long they're retained? Our security policy requires seven years for certain transaction audit trails.
[01:44] Miguel: By default hosted audit logs are retained 90 days in the console and you can export to your SIEM (S3/Cloudwatch/ELK) — retention configurable; for Dedicated/Private we can set up streaming to your tenant and retention policy up to multi-year if needed. The logs come with requestID, model, route, userID (if forwarded), latency, and token counts.
[01:59] Karen: Are those logs tamper-evident? We need attestable chains for forensic requests.
[02:04] Jun: we have write-once export patterns and you can configure log delivery to an S3 bucket with object-lock for immutability or to your audit cluster. Also we can sign logs for integrity.
[02:14] Karen: Good. Next SSO — we use Okta and want SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. What's the integration surface?
[02:21] Miguel: Full SAML SSO supported, SCIM for provisioning. We provide SP metadata and support IdP-initiated flows; for Dedicated/Private we can also do SAML over a private connection.
[02:31] Darren: Any gotchas with claims mapping and groups to RBAC? We need AD groups to map to roles like observer, dev, admin.
[02:38] Miguel: You can map SAML groups to RBAC roles. There's a role matrix in the docs; Jun can show an example of least-privilege roles — e.g., model-rater, inference-operator, billing-viewer.
[02:49] Karen: We need granular separation — devs can't call production models, ops only view certain logs. Can you do route-level permissions?
[02:56] Jun: yes you can create per-route policies and tie them to roles; we also support token scoping where API tokens are limited to model families and routes. There is audit trail per-token.
[03:07] Maya: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys / BYOK and HSM backed KMS?
[03:12] Miguel: Yes. Hosted supports BYOK via integration with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS or Google CMEK). Dedicated and Private support HSM-backed keys and on-prem KMS, including split-key and rotating keys. We can do key-rotation policies and hold key ownership with the customer.
[03:26] Darren: For BYOK, how does the traffic flow? Are keys touching Redwood machines? We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[03:32] Jun: the pattern is envelope encryption: Redwood stores encrypted model artifacts and object metadata encrypted with a data key that is wrapped by your KMS. The unwrapped key is only in memory on the host if you run Private; for Hosted we use a KMS gateway pattern where unwrap is done in a customer-managed KMS or HSM with a remote attestation. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[03:51] Karen: Sounds like we need an architecture diagram with the trust boundaries highlighted.
[03:55] Miguel: we'll include that.
[03:57] Aisha: On data retention and deletion, what options exist? They want legal hold and ability to redact.
[04:03] Miguel: We have a deletion workflow — you can request dataset erasure, which triggers encrypted-object deletion and purge of caches. For Hosted, there is a 24-72 hour deletion window depending on backups, and for Dedicated/Private we can do immediate wipe policies and provide certificate of deletion. For legal hold we can do snapshot holds and prevent automatic purge.
[04:22] Darren: Are there backups stored offsite with a different retention schedule? We need to ensure backups also get rotated/deleted per request.
[04:27] Jun: yes backups have their own retention; in dedicated/private we align backup retention to customer policy and can rotate them under customer KMS. We'll provide backup policy docs.
[04:37] Karen: On compliance evidence, besides SOC2 do you have artifact-level mapping — e.g., control to config paths? Our vendor team wants a control matrix.
[04:45] Miguel: we have a control-mapping doc (SOC2 control to Redwood config and docs). We'll send that and a sample config for RBAC + SAML.
[04:53] Maya: Legal will want the DPA and some standard indemnities. Any known restrictions on data residency we should flag?
[04:59] Aisha: Hosted supports multiple regions, we can lock to region; Dedicated is region-specific; Private gives you on-prem. We'll surface the subprocessor list by region.
[05:09] Darren: On latency & model serving, one last ops question — if we go Dedicated, can we get reserved GPU pools and guarantee latency?
[05:16] Miguel: yes Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with SLA options; you can configure autoscaling and burst off to hosted if you want fallback. We'll provide performance profiles per model / sequence length.
[05:25] Karen: Any red flags re: PCI scope? We don't want card data in logs or model inputs.
[05:30] Jun: we recommend tokenization on ingest and you can configure scrubbing of PII from logs. There's a built-in post-processor to drop or hash fields before persistence.
[05:40] Darren: Great. For the pilot we're likely to do a 2-week Dedicated test in our dev VPC, with BYOK KMS, SAML integration and limited RBAC roles. We need to run a short benchmark and security review.
[05:50] Miguel: That aligns with our standard pilot — we typically provision a small dedicated pool, provide test credentials, and run the benchmark together. We'll need your Okta test tenant and a contact for KMS side.
[05:59] Aisha: recapping next steps — i'll send SOC2 + pentest summary and the standard security FAQ; Miguel will send network diagram, RBAC matrix, and SAML metadata; Darren will spin up Okta test and share creds; Maya will share DPA asks. We'll schedule the deep technical bench session for next week.
[06:20] Karen: sounds good, thanks.
[06:23] Maya: thanks all.
[06:25] Aisha: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite.
